sentences.text:
This Writ Petition, under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, is filed by the petitioners seeking the following relief:
"....to issue order or orders, direction or directions, writ or writs more particularly one in the nature of Writ of Mandamus declaring the action of the respondents in not determining the market value of petitioners land situated in Sy.Nos.65/2, 109/2,
110/2, 111/2, 85/2, 110/2 and 59/2 total an extent of Acs.4.14 guntas dry lands of Thakkasila Village, Alampur Mandal, Mahabubnagar District, as per the judgment in O.P.No.19 of 2006 dt.22.01.2009 and subsequently representations made by the petitioners on 13.05.2009 under Section 28-A of Land Acquisition Act, consequently direct the respondents to pay the market value with all the statutory benefit in accordance with the market value fixed by Hon'ble Senior Civil Judge, Gadwal in O.P.No.19 of 2006 and to pass such other order..."

2. The case of the petitioners is that they are the marginal farmers and owners of small extents of lands in Sy.Nos.65/2, 109/2, 110/2, 111/2, 85/2, 110/2 and 59/2, total Acs.4.14 guntas of dry lands,
situated at Thakkasila Village, Alampur Mandal, Mahabubnagar District.
A notification was issued under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short, 'the Act') on 11.01.2005.
After following the due procedure, an Award was passed on 31.08.2005.

Not satisfied with the Award being passed by the respondents, the petitioners have made an application/representation dated 13.05.2009 under Section 28-A of the Act seeking to fix the market value as determined in O.P.No.19 of 2006 for similar lands acquired under very same notification.

3. The grievance of the petitioners is that even though they submitted representation dated 13.05.2009, the respondents have not paid the compensation in terms of Section 28-A of the Act to the petitioners.
4. Learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition has not disputed the submission of the application/representation by the petitioners.

5. It is stated by the learned counsel for the petitioners that for the lands acquired by the very same notification having similar potentialities, compensation was enhanced in O.P.No.19 of 2006 vide decree and judgment, dated 22.01.2009 and immediately after coming to know about the said judgment, the petitioners made representation dated 13.05.2009 under Section 28-A of the Act annexing certified copy of the said judgment.
Seshamma

The application submitted by the petitioners to enhance the compensation, as enhanced in O.P.No.19 of 2006, is pending since 15 years and the respondents have not filed counter-affidavit denying the entitlement of the petitioners for payment of compensation on par with the claimants in O.P.No.19 of 2006.

7. In view of the same, the respondents are directed to consider the representation/application submitted by the petitioners for fixation of market value for their lands on par with the lands acquired by the very same notification, within a period of three (3) months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
8.
With the above direction, the Writ Petition is disposed of.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in this Writ Petition shall stand closed.

_ _ JUSTICE C.V. BHASKAR REDDY Date:
